title: CI: cache provenance and reproducible artifact signing
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Introduce explicit cache provenance metadata and reproducible signing for CI artifacts to make builds auditable, enable safe cache reuse across runners, and meet emerging compliance needs. This ticket implements a minimal, incremental flow: attach deterministic provenance to cached build layers and signed SBOMs/artifacts produced by CI so consumers (runtime teams, security, and infra) can verify origin and content without re-running expensive builds.
background: Our current CI caching is opaque: cache hits are based on blob keys that rarely carry human- or tool-readable provenance, causing uncertainty when debugging flakiness and making security audits harder. Several internal incidents showed mismatches between expected and produced artifacts after cache warmups. In addition, regulated customers and internal compliance ask for verifiable artifact provenance and SBOMs for release artifacts. We also want to avoid blowing up CI runtime by doing full image re-builds for verification.
scope: 1) Extend CI cache keys and metadata store to include provenance fields (git sha, builder image id, toolchain digest, build-profile) 2) Emit reproducible SBOM and a lightweight signature (SLSA-like attestation) for build outputs 3) Add tooling to verify signatures and provenance in downstream jobs and the release pipeline 4) Update selected build pipelines (js, go, python) as pilots.
out_of_scope: 1) Full org-wide migration of all language runners (will follow pilots) 2) Hardware-backed signing (HSM) in this ticket — we will use ephemeral GPG or keyless proofs as interim approach 3) Changes to artifact retention policy beyond what is required for provenance tags.
acceptance_criteria: CI cache entries include provenance metadata and are visible in the build trace/logs
At least one JS, Go, and Python pipeline produce an SBOM alongside the build artifact and publish a deterministic signature
Downstream verification job can validate provenance and signature without rebuilding the artifact
Confluence runbook documents the verification workflow and commands
Security review sign-off obtained for signing approach and key management plan
technical_notes: Cache provenance fields: {repo, git_sha, builder_digest, build_profile, toolchain_digests, timestamp} — timestamp used only for human traceability, not cache key determinism
Deterministic SBOM: use Syft with fixed seed and ordered output to avoid non-determinism across runs
Signing: prototype with in-repo ephemeral GPG key + CI-kept keypair for pilot; plan for keyless signing via Sigstore in follow-up
Cache key computation: primary key remains deterministic digest of inputs; provenance is attached as metadata not used for hit calculation to avoid churn; add optional strict mode for validation runs
Storage: add small provenance JSON blobs (<1KB) to our existing remote cache index; cost estimates ~5-15GB/month for org-wide metadata at current build volume
Verification tool: small CLI (go) to fetch artifact, SBOM, and signature, verify signature and compare recorded provenance to actual inputs
Rollout: start with non-critical pipelines and a feature flag to enable strict validation for canary releases
migration_plan: Week 1: implement cache metadata schema + CI step to emit provenance for prototype pipelines (ENG branch)
Week 2: wire SBOM generation and signature step; create verification CLI and add to CI image
Week 3: pilot on js-frontend, go-build-service, python-sdk pipelines; collect metrics on CI time and cache hit rates
Week 4: integrate verification check into release pipeline and write runbook; request security review
Post-pilot: iterate on storage lifecycle and evaluate Sigstore integration for production signing
risks: Increased CI runtime: additional SBOM and signing steps may add 10-25% to build time for piloted pipelines
Cache churn: if provenance is naively included in the cache key, hit rates will drop — implementation must attach metadata separately
Key management: using ephemeral CI keys for pilot increases risk surface; must get security sign-off and rotate keys frequently
Verification false positives: non-deterministic SBOMs could cause spurious validation failures — need strict reproducibility testing
Storage costs: added metadata increases remote cache index size and S3 GET/PUT operations
